name: National Dairy Shrine Scholarship
description: For students pursuing dairy science, animal science, or agriculture degrees. Multiple scholarship funds available. Strong relevance to Ohio students from dairy farming families in Wayne, Holmes, and Darke counties.

description: For students pursuing foodservice management, culinary arts, or hospitality degrees. Ohio has a large restaurant and hospitality sector. Awards based on industry work experience and academic achievement.

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers Scholarship
description: For students pursuing chemical engineering degrees. Multiple AIChE scholarships and awards. Ohio has strong ChemE programs at OSU, Case Western, and University of Akron.

name: Air & Waste Management Association Scholarship

name: Ohio Bankers League Foundation Scholarship
description: For Ohio students pursuing finance, business, economics, or banking careers. The OBL Foundation supports students interested in Ohio's financial services industry. Check for local bank scholarships through your own bank.

name: Ohio FFA Foundation Scholarship
description: Multiple scholarships for Ohio FFA members pursuing agriculture, natural resources, and related degrees. Ohio FFA Foundation partners with agricultural businesses and associations to offer 100+ scholarship opportunities annually.

name: Ohio Hospitality Association Scholarship
description: For Ohio students pursuing culinary arts, foodservice management, hotel management, or tourism. Ohio has a $28+ billion hospitality industry. Awards recognize work experience, leadership, and academic merit.

name: Mercer County Community Foundation Scholarship
description: Scholarships for Celina and Mercer County, Ohio students. Mercer County is one of Ohio's top agricultural counties. Foundation awards multiple funds based on merit, need, and field of study.

demographics: Mercer County, OH residents or students

description: Scholarships for West Union and Adams County, Ohio students. One of the smaller Ohio county foundations, but offers meaningful local support for students from this rural southwestern Ohio community.

name: American Water Works Association Scholarship
description: For students pursuing environmental science, civil engineering, or water resources careers. Ohio's Great Lakes location makes water resource management particularly relevant. AWWA Ohio Section also offers local awards.

name: Hagan Scholarship
description: Helps high-achieving students with financial need graduate college debt-free. Up to $7,500 per semester for 8 semesters, plus $2,000 for college essentials. Parents’ household income must not exceed $125,000. Application opens September 1.

name: Prudential Emerging Visionaries
description: Recognizes young people ages 14–18 for innovative solutions to financial and societal challenges. 25 winners receive $5,000 plus an all-expenses-paid trip to Prudential headquarters; grand prize adds $10,000. Successor to the Spirit of Community Awards.

name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
description: Awards renewable $5,000 scholarships (up to $20,000 total) to high school seniors who demonstrate courage, strength, and wisdom in achieving their goals. Successor to the AXA Achievement Scholarship. Apply early — selection considers first-come applications.

name: NSA Stokes Educational Scholarship
description: Up to $30,000 per year for high school seniors planning to major in computer science or computer/electrical engineering. Includes paid summer work at NSA and guaranteed employment after graduation (service commitment applies).

name: Carson Scholars Program
description: Recognizes students in grades 9–11 who excel academically (3.75+ GPA) and are committed to community service. Winners receive a $1,000 college scholarship held in trust. Requires nomination by an educator at your school — ask a teacher or counselor.

name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
description: For high school seniors who demonstrate leadership, drive, integrity, and citizenship. $10,000 renewable for up to four years — $40,000 total per recipient.

name: Ohio State Morrill Scholarship Program
description: Ohio State’s premier diversity/leadership scholarship — awards range from full in-state tuition to the full cost of attendance. Apply for admission by the November 1 early action deadline and complete the MSP essay.
amount_display: Full tuition up to full cost of attendance

name: Miami University Merit Scholarships
description: Merit awards ranging from $2,000 per year up to full tuition for incoming freshmen. No separate application — apply for admission by the December 1 priority deadline to be automatically considered.

name: Lisa Kaminski Scholarship
description: One-time $4,000 grant for Greater Cincinnati area seniors (including Northern Kentucky) with outstanding community service who plan to major in STEM — technology fields like computer science, MIS, data analytics, and digital design strongly encouraged. Two recommendations required; women candidates receive preference as a tiebreaker.

name: Cincinnati Scholarship Foundation Scholarship
description: Awards 140+ scholarships and $2.5M each year to students from the Greater Cincinnati region (Butler, Clermont, Hamilton, and Warren counties in OH; plus Dearborn IN and Boone, Campbell, Kenton KY) with financial need. Typical award $1,000 per semester for up to 8 semesters. Application opens each January.

name: UC Marian Spencer Scholarship
description: Full tuition, housing, and food at UC — plus study abroad, co-op support, mentoring, and career coaching — for 10 Cincinnati Public Schools students each year. Eligible students are in the top 10% of their senior class (15% for Walnut Hills). Apply for UC admission by November 1.

name: UC Cincinnati Pride Grant
description: Covers full tuition plus a book allowance for Cincinnati Public Schools graduates who are Pell Grant eligible. No GPA requirement — just graduate from CPS, complete the FAFSA, and be admitted to UC by March 1.

name: UC Gen-1 Program
description: For first-generation college students (neither parent has a bachelor’s degree) who are Pell-eligible: $2,000 per semester while living on campus, plus an unlimited meal plan for the first year and dedicated support programming. Apply to UC by December 1.

name: Miami University Cincinnati Scholars (Bridges)
description: Full cost of attendance (minus expected family contribution and $3,500 self-help) for Cincinnati-area students. Requires 3.0+ GPA or top 25% of class, rigorous coursework, and leadership involvement. Attend the fall Bridges program (apply by late September) and apply for admission by December 1.

name: University of Dayton Flyer Promise
description: Covers all tuition plus up to $7,500 toward housing and meals for students from partner high schools (including Cincinnati and Dayton public schools). Requires 3.0+ GPA, family income of $75,000 or less, and Pell eligibility. Apply for admission by December 1.

name: Cincinnati State Be Great Grant
organization: Cincinnati State Technical and Community College
description: Up to $1,000 toward tuition plus $1,000 for books for Cincinnati Public Schools and CYC high school graduates enrolling full-time as first-time freshmen. Pell-eligible students qualify — rolling deadline, apply any time.

name: Woman’s City Club of Greater Cincinnati Scholarship
organization: Woman’s City Club of Greater Cincinnati
description: Small local award for female high school seniors in the Greater Cincinnati area. Requires an essay and a letter of recommendation — with far fewer applicants than national scholarships, local awards like this are some of the easiest to win.

name: Vietnam Veterans of America Chapter 10 Scholarship
description: For veterans and their immediate family members or dependents from the Greater Cincinnati area — high school seniors or current college/vocational students. A small local award with a limited applicant pool.

name: Mason Scholarship Foundation
description: Founded in 1983 by the Kiwanis Club of Mason, awards two- and four-year scholarships to high school seniors residing in the Mason (OH) school district. Applications open each winter — get the form from the MHS counseling office or the Kiwanis website.
